answer: Magistrate appointment with court sitting record is the check: sittings recorded at one court for years. A farm faking 243 aliases needs 243 separate sitting records, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. Call it the juniper rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the timber record is open for audit, and the fable window is too short for 243 aliases to earn their price back.
